findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing credentials to anyone with access to the instance or state file.

The EBS volume does not have encryption enabled (encrypted attribute is commented out), leaving data at rest unprotected and exposed if the underlying storage is compromised or the volume/snapshot is shared.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted EBS volume and has no encryption configured, meaning any exported or shared snapshot would expose the underlying data unprotected.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from any host on the internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted egress to all destinations, broadening the attack surface for the web instance and permitting unrestricted outbound traffic which could aid data exfiltration.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially exposing sensitive network traffic logs to unauthorized access.

The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched here (including the web_host with an open security group) to automatically receive public IPs, increasing direct internet exposure.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instances launched in it, increasing exposure to the internet.
